page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor architecture running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware includes 256.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, placing it in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached read-only bandwidth ranking in the top 10% and large-block read/write bandwidth in the top 25%. The CPU's instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration, support strong performance in encryption, physics simulations, and software compilation. Redis SET operations and medium-model LLM text generation also achieve top-tier throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for enterprise-grade general-purpose workloads. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention, though the lack of bundled local storage requires external storage provisioning. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
